subject: Discovery readout & trial run playbook — next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aiden Clarke <aiden.clarke@atlasiq.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery readout & trial run playbook — next steps

Hi Aiden / Naomi —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so everyone has the same playbook for the 30-day trial we discussed. I captured the core pain, the measurable goals, proposed scope, and immediate access asks below. Please confirm anything I missed.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Intake noise: high volume of patient intake forms with inconsistent structure, causing downstream triage delays.
- Model drift on entity extraction across clinic subtypes; manual review costs are high.
- Need for deterministic (explainable) reranking for triage prioritization.

Primary goals for a successful 30-day trial:
- Precision gain: +12% F1 on discharge_reason entity extraction vs baseline.
- Latency target: p95 generation latency <250ms for 512-token prompts.
- Cost target: <= $0.003/token average with batching & caching tuned.

Proposed trial scope (what we'll run in the first 30 days):
1) Data slice: 10k de-identified intake records (release 1 of sample set) for prompt engineering and evals.
2) Prompt/eval plan: 4 prompt families (entity extraction, triage score, clinical summary, rerank), each with 200 labeled examples for litmus tests + continuous eval harness.
3) Serving config: start on Hosted Redwood API with a dedicated trial instance using quantized model variant (v2-q8) — fall back to medium model if latency SLOs fail.
4) Success gating: stoplight criteria mapped to the metrics above; handoff doc for productionization if criteria met.

Immediate action items (owners & timing):
- AtlasIQ: provide de-identified sample CSV (10k rows) and a short schema doc by Mon, Apr 26. (Aiden)
- Redwood: provide trial playbook + access role (IAM) and initial prompt templates by Thu, Apr 24. (Monica)
- Redwood: supply evaluation harness and baseline scripts (to reproduce current extraction metric) by Thu, Apr 24. (Marissa)
- Checkpoint: synchronous 30-min alignment call on Fri, Apr 30 to review first eval pass.

Attachments: atlasiq_requirements_v1.xlsx (sample schema we reviewed) — will drop full playbook in a follow-up.

Open questions for AtlasIQ:
- Can you confirm export format (CSV vs NDJSON) and whether records include timezones?
- Any regulatory constraints we should model in the trial (PII masking rules beyond our default)?

If that looks right I’ll open the trial environment and share credentials + the Redwood trial playbook.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: atlasiq_requirements_v1.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)]

Vivek —

This is perfect, thanks for summarizing. Quick clarifications:
- We’ll export CSV (comma-delimited), and the records include UTC timestamps — I’ll flag any clinic-local times in a separate column.
- On masking: we can provide 10k de-identified rows with hashed MRNs and fully removed free-text PII; we will keep the clinician notes but can redact patient names.

One small ask: could you include an evaluation rubric for "clinical summary quality"? We typically find ROUGE/EM insufficient for clinical concision. If you can propose a human-rated scale prototype (1-5) we’ll run that in parallel.

Aiden
Director of Data Science, AtlasIQ

Hi Aiden / Naomi —

Thanks — we’ll do the human-rated clinical summary rubric and drop it into the playbook. Quick operational notes to make the onboarding smooth:

Access & account setup (what we need from AtlasIQ):
- S3 read-only bucket or an upload link for the 10k CSV (preferred); if S3, grant the role redwood-trial-ingest@atlasiq with GetObject permissions for that specific bucket/prefix.
- HubSpot record confirmation so we can attach the trial workspace: ATQ-2027-179 (please confirm).
- Point of contact for VPN whitelisting (if you want Redwood Private staging access later).

Trial environment we’ll provision:
- Hosted trial instance (v2-q8) with 16GB KV cache and 2 worker nodes to start.
- Evaluation harness: will run nightly batch evals with the 4 prompt families and push results to the shared drive.
- Observability: we’ll enable model-level tracing and the prompt-level cost breakdown.

Success criteria & metrics (quick reference):
- Entity extraction: +12% F1 vs your baseline after prompt tuning (200 examples per family).
- Clinical summary: human-rated avg >=3.8/5 on our proposed rubric with no more than 8% hallucination rate in a 200-example sample.
- Triage rerank: precision@5 >= baseline +10% for urgent cases.
- Stability: 72-hour rolling p95 latency <250ms and no more than 3% error rate.

Deliverables we are attaching now: Redwood trial playbook (PDF) with the eval rubric + initial prompt templates.

Let me know when the CSV is staged and I’ll kick off ingestion.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
